items.followUp: A body of weight 30 N accelerates vertically upward at 3 m s⁻². Find the applied force. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The weight and gravitational field strength give the body's mass through W = mg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mass calculation.

rubric.why: The applied force must overcome the weight and provide the upward net force ma.
rubric.description: Sets up Newton’s second law for upward motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct force equation.

rubric.why: Substituting the mass, acceleration and weight gives the applied force expression.
The applied force is the sum of the weight and ma.
rubric.description: Calculates the required force as 24 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical result.

rubric.why: The required force must act upward to produce the stated upward acceleration.
rubric.description: States the force’s direction as upward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the 24 N force as upward.

modelAnswer: Given: W = 20 N, a = 2 m s⁻²; take g = 10 m s⁻².
Using W = mg, m = W/g = 20 N ÷ 10 m s⁻² = 2 kg.
For upward motion, F − W = ma, so F = ma + W.

items.followUp: A metal block measures 20 cm × 10 cm × 5 cm and has a mass of 2.7 kg. Find its density in kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: The dimensions are converted to SI units before calculating density in SI units.
rubric.description: Converts all three dimensions to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI dimensions.

rubric.why: The volume is the product of the block’s three dimensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume and unit.

rubric.why: The mass must be expressed in kilograms for the SI density calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mass conversion.

rubric.why: Density is defined as mass divided by volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Dividing 0.850 kg by 0.002 m³ gives 425 kg m⁻³.
rubric.description: Finds the density with the correct SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: length = 40 cm = 0.40 m, width = 10 cm = 0.10 m, height = 5 cm = 0.05 m, mass = 850 g = 0.850 kg.
Volume, V = length × width × height = (0.40 m)(0.10 m)(0.05 m) = 0.002 m³.

rubric.why: Moving the decimal five places to the right gives a coefficient between 1 and 10, so the power is −5.
Moving the decimal eight places to the left gives a coefficient between 1 and 10, so the power is 8.
